closest_works.citation: Hirschman 1970, Exit, Voice, and Loyalty, ch.4 pp.51–55
closest_works.shared_claim: Selective exit drains voice; mechanism inherited.
closest_works.difference: Conditional separation of valid renewal jurisdiction from enduring accountability to experimental subjects after lost membership.

closest_works.citation: Kuyper 2013, Designing institutions for global democracy, pp.198–203
closest_works.shared_claim: Exit and sunset/renegotiation provisions support experiments and correction.
closest_works.difference: Counterexample where membership loss makes renewal unable to fulfill original review assurance despite two valid votes; does not apply where temporary escape retains standing.

closest_works.citation: Goodin 2024, Proximity Principle, Adieu, opening sections
closest_works.shared_claim: Jurisdiction and franchise must track morally relevant relations, not merely geography.
closest_works.difference: Issue-specific trial-accountability process without freezing electorate for future governance; promise/continuity ground rather than general franchise expansion.

closest_works.citation: Farrow 2007, European Constitutionalism and Retrospective Legitimacy, pp.10–13
closest_works.shared_claim: Later democratic acceptance need not legitimate earlier institutional imposition.
closest_works.difference: Grants unanimous trial consent and valid renewal; identifies failure of retained review rights in between.
Compatible prospective benefit does not alone settle past accountability; full-paper overlap uncertain.

limitations: Bounded English search and selected primary excerpts, not absolute novelty. Francis abstract only; Goodin 2007 inaccessible. Elementary selection bias and persistence of obligations are not claimed new. Independent critic must decide whether the conjunction yields sufficient contribution.
